notes:
The Eduard Zelmer family immigrated from Russia back to Germany prior to 1910.  It has been suggested, by Olga Lee (nee Zelmer) that the family had been promised land in Germany but their father, Eduard, turned it down.  There is a comment that the German Government allowed them to re-enter and received them, and it appears that they did in fact take up land (assumption, as tenants) and engaged in farming in general, including fruit farming.  I (Allan Zelmer) can recall my father (Oscar Zelmer) saying that he was required to fetch cattle from their pasture area and that it was common for him and others to take along potatoes to roast in an open fire as their food.  He also said that while there was much fruit grown in the area, the local folk knew little or nothing about using fruit for baking, such as in pies etc.

From details that Rose obtained from Olga, it appears that the reason for their father, Eduard, leaving Germany, is that he was unwilling or unable, to give up money for his wife's (Velte) brother's land.  I don't really understand this remark but Olga has now passed on and clarification is not possible.  I am told that we still have relatives there.  They attended a Lutheran Church in Germany.

On July 16, 1910, Eduard immigrated to Canada along with his wife Emilie, Adela, Amalie, Oscar, Olga and Antonia on the SS Kronprinz Friedrich Wilhelm.  He entered at Ellis Island in New York, and then by train (to Montreal?) and eventually to Winnipeg.

The following are the addresses of dwellings the Zelmer family rented in Winnipeg.  This data was provided by Leon Schneider (from memory) while he and my Aunt Rose shared a weekend with us at our cottage at Brereton Lake in August of 1984; and a very cold one I might add:

- 699 Burrows Avenue (Note: On Nov. 9/96, Lorna and Allan drove to Burrows Ave and found that
          there is no such address.)
- 692 Atlantic Avenue (The 1914 and 1915 issue of Henderson Guide confirms Eduard Zelmer living here.) (Rose Zelmer was born here)
- McKenzie Avenue (Couldn't locate due no specific address.)
- St. John's Avenue (Couldn't locate due no specific address.)
- 846 Aberdeen Avenue, near Sinclair St.
- 692 Mountain Avenue. This was at Mountain and Parr.  Eduard Zelmer died there at the age of 54 in February of 1930.

Interestingly, Allan Zelmer attended Michael Faraday school which was directly opposite this house and never knew it was the former dwelling place of his grandparents. This address has been verified by the Winnipeg Free Press obituary of Eduard Zelmer.

Also puzzling is the fact that for the thousands of times our family travelled up and down Mountain Ave., I can never recall my father (Oscar) ever mentioning that this house had once been the home of his parents.  He did however mention Atlantic Ave. but did not give me the address. Somehow, I think
he said that Atlantic Ave. was the first place they occupied after arriving from overseas on their immigration trip.

- Ellice & Hargrave, Devonshire Apartments.
- Victor Street. (Couldn't locate due no specific address.)
- Mountain Avenue & Main Street. (Same as above.)
- 378 Parr Street, between College and Mountain on the west side.
- Manitoba & Battery - Northwest corner.
- Burrows & Powers - First house.
- 689 Bannerman.

-Allan Zelmer

Obituary from Winnipeg Free Press archives Nov. 5/96 indicates age as 53 years. Cause of death is not known, but I do know that my Grandfather fell from a tower on the site of the Manitoba Bridge & Iron Works. Thereafter (2 years?) he became ill and died. Family members do not seem to know the cause, however there was a suggestion of cancer resulting from the fall. The family at the time lived at 692 Mountain Ave.

-Allan Zelmer
